newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU ROCKED FOR FIRST LOSS AS A YANKEE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU ROCKED FOR FIRST LOSS AS A YANKEE.

text.p: Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu gave up six runs and seven hits in taking his first loss in the major leagues as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the New York Yankees 6-2 on Sunday.
Dave Nilsson had the big blow for the Brewers, hitting a two-run homer to highlight a four-run third inning. He added an RBI double in the fifth.

Irabu (2-1), who lasted 6-2/3 innings, struggled for the second straight start, and has surrendered four home runs in 18-1/3 innings. He has given up 11 runs in 11 2/3 innings in his last two starts, raising his ERA to 6.38.

"I got behind the hitters and made my pitch too good," Irabu said through an interpreter in explaining Nilsson's home run. "I can't put my pitches over the middle of the plate to major league hitters."
"His fast ball is not 97 miles an hour," Nilsson said. "His split is his best pitch. He will be a good pitcher but he has a lot to learn about keeping runners on."

In Anaheim, Luis Alicea had three hits and three RBI and Chuck Finley tied a career high with his fifth straight victory as the Angels rolled to their 12th win in 13 games, a 9-5 decision over the Toronto Blue Jays.
Darin Erstad also had three hits and scored three times for the Angels, who have come from behind in half of their 54 wins this season.
Alicea launched a two-run homer, his fifth, to lift the Angels into a 3-3 tie in the fourth. He added an RBI single in a two-run sixth and doubled and scored the game's final run in the eighth.

In Seattle, Bob Wells held Kansas City without a hit over the final 2 1/3 innings to record his first major league save and Dan Wilson drove in two runs to lead the Mariners to a 5-4 victory over the Royals.
Wilson delivered RBI singles in the second and fifth innings, helping the Mariners open a 5-1 advantage.
Seattle's Jamie Moyer (10-3) scattered nine hits to win for the ninth time in his last 10 starts.

At Texas, Rusty Greer hit a two-out homer in the bottom of the 10th inning as the Rangers overcame a five-run deficit for a 7-6 victory over the Detroit Tigers, salvaging the final game of their three-game series.

After Mark McLemore and Ivan Rodriguez grounded out, Greer drove A.J. Sager's 0-1 pitch over the scoreboard in left field for his 14th home run. It was the third time this season Greer has had a game-winning RBI in the Rangers' last at-bat.
John Wetteland (5-2) allowed a single to Tony Clark in the top of the 10th, but struck out the side.
In Oakland, Brad Radke pitched a five-hitter for his ninth straight win and the Minnesota Twins beat the Athletics, 1-0, to complete their first three-game sweep in Oakland in 18 years.
The Twins have won four straight games and six of their last seven while Oakland has lost 11 of 15.

In Baltimore, Jaime Navarro came within two outs of a shutout and Frank Thomas and Norberto Martin each drove in two runs in a five-run second inning as the Chicago White Sox thrashed the slumping Orioles, 10-2.
Navarro (8-8) lost his bid for a shutout when Tony Tarasco hit a two-run homer with one out in the ninth. He walked one and struck out four for his second complete game of the season.
Thomas added a two-run homer in the eighth.
Baltimore third baseman Cal Ripken was ejected for only the third time in his career for arguing balls and strikes in the second inning.
In Cleveland, Charles Nagy (10-6) pitched seven strong innings to help the Indians beat the Red Sox, 7-2, and snap Boston's four-game winning streak.

Cleveland, which has split its last six games following a 7-1 stretch, maintained its 4 1/2-game lead over the White Sox in the American League Central. Indians manager Mike Hargrove recorded his 500th major league win.
